subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Testimonials and Trust
description: A 60-second lesson on Testimonials and Trust.

hook.text: A landing page added three customer testimonials. Conversion jumped 34%. The product was unchanged.

buildup.text: Testimonials reduce uncertainty. When you see someone like you succeeded, you assume the product will work for you too.

discovery.text: Similarity matters most. A testimonial from someone matching your age, job, and problem outperforms a celebrity.

twist.text: Fake testimonials are widespread. Stock photos, invented names, and paid reviews exploit trust at scale.

climax.text: Check testimonials for specifics. Real reviews mention details. Fake ones stay vague and generic.

punchline.text: Trust the story with details. Skip the praise without proof.

quiz.question: What makes testimonials most persuasive?
options: Testimonials from people similar to the potential buyer
The total number of testimonials regardless of content
